# Welcome {.unnumbered}

Cleaning messy psychology survey data with R & the tidyverse — work your way from raw export to analysable dataset.

::: {.badge-row}
`dplyr` `tidyr` `readr` `lubridate` `janitor` `naniar` `here`
:::

## How to use this {.unnumbered}

Data cleaning usually follows a fairly consistent set of steps — from setting up your project, through importing and checking your data, to saving a clean version ready for analysis. You can work through those steps in order from start to finish, or jump straight to whichever task matches what you're stuck on right now — whatever's useful for your data today. Each section ends with real R code you can copy into your script, plus a tip about why it matters.

Before you start, install the packages once: `install.packages(c("tidyverse", "janitor", "naniar", "here", "DataExplorer"))`. Then at the top of every cleaning script: `library(tidyverse)` loads dplyr, tidyr, readr, and lubridate together; add `library(janitor)`, `library(naniar)`, `library(here)` and `library(DataExplorer)` separately.

Start every project as an **RStudio Project** with separate folders for raw and clean data, and use `here()` to build file paths (e.g. `here("data", "raw", "survey_raw.csv")`) instead of typing them out by hand — see [Set up your project](01-setup.qmd).
